nhl.xg_for.label: Team expected goals for (shot quality created), strength-split and adjusted
nhl.xg_for.mechanism: Expected goals credit the quality and location of shots a team generates, so xGF measures offensive process with far less shooting-luck noise than goals.
nhl.xg_for.rationale: Goals are rare and luck-heavy; xG stabilises much faster and is the best public repeatable measure of offence. Subtle: public xG models omit passing/pre-shot movement and goalie quality, treat all shooters equally, and are biased by rink scorer inconsistency in shot location. Use it split by 5v5 / PP and adjust for opponent and for score effects, since trailing teams inflate volume.
nhl.xg_for.measurement: Per-60 xGF at 5v5 (score-and-venue adjusted) and on PP, as exponentially weighted averages (half-life ~25-40 games) shrunk toward league mean with a prior sized by games played; adjust for opponent by regressing team-game xGF on offence and defence team effects plus home indicator (ridge). Report separate 5v5 and special-teams components rather than one blended number.

nhl.xg_against.label: Team expected goals against (shot suppression quality)
nhl.xg_against.mechanism: Expected goals against measure the quality and quantity of chances a team's skaters allow, independent of whether the goalie happened to stop them.
nhl.xg_against.rationale: Separates defensive process (what the skaters control) from goaltending outcome; critical for totals, team totals and for estimating what shot quality a goalie will face. Subtle: xGA as published is goalie-neutral, so any goalie-specific adjustment must be layered on top, and defensive effects partly reflect personnel (injuries to top pair) that stale season averages hide.
nhl.xg_against.measurement: Per-60 xGA at 5v5 and on PK, score/venue-adjusted, exponentially weighted with opponent adjustment via the same ridge team-effects model as xG for; recompute with lineup-weighted projection (replace absent defencemen with replacement-level impact) for the specific game.

nhl.pace.label: Shot-attempt rate / event pace (combined attempts per 60)
nhl.pace.mechanism: A game's total shot-attempt volume (both teams) sets the number of chances available, which scales shots on goal, saves, and total goals.
nhl.pace.rationale: Pace is a team style trait (system, forecheck, trap) and a matchup trait: two high-event teams exceed the sum of their parts, two trap teams undershoot. Subtle: pace changes with score effects and special-teams time, and is partly a coaching-system effect that moves after coaching changes, so long averages lag.
nhl.pace.measurement: Combined Corsi attempts per 60 for team A offence plus team B defence (and vice versa) using opponent-adjusted team effects; track team-level 'event rate' (attempts for + against per 60) with EWMA; include rink-specific scorer bias correction.

nhl.special_teams.label: Power-play and penalty-kill efficiency (xG-based) and special-teams matchup
nhl.special_teams.mechanism: Special teams convert penalties into goals at far higher rates than 5v5, so unit quality and opponent PK structure shift team goals and totals.
nhl.special_teams.rationale: The PP xGF/60 of the unit and the PK xGA/60 of the opponent combine multiplicatively with expected PP opportunities. Subtle: raw PP% is dominated by shooting luck and sample size; xG-based rates plus personnel (injury to PP1 quarterback) are far more repeatable. Use regressed rates and account for aggressive vs passive PK shapes.
nhl.special_teams.measurement: PP xGF/60 and PK xGA/60 from last ~40 games, EWMA, shrunk to league mean; combine as expected PP goals = (team A PP xGF rate adj for opp PK) x (expected PP minutes from penalties model); replace personnel when key unit members out.

nhl.goalie_start.label: Confirmed starting goalie (timestamped) and its pregame probability
nhl.goalie_start.mechanism: The starting goalie determines the goal-prevention quality of the whole game and defines saves-market eligibility, so which goalie plays shifts goals, totals, winners and saves lines.
nhl.goalie_start.rationale: Starter identity is the single largest in-day information event in NHL pricing. Subtle: confirmation often arrives after morning skate (late morning to ~1 hr before puck drop) and some starters are only confirmed via lineup card; markets may be open before confirmation, so any model has to carry a start probability (back-to-back, recent rest pattern) and reprice on the news. A goalie who starts but is pulled early still settles his saves market on partial saves.
nhl.goalie_start.measurement: Record every source's announcement with timestamp; before confirmation model P(starter) from rest days, back-to-back second-game rate, consecutive starts, coach pattern; after confirmation set to 1. Feed downstream models both goalie identity and confirmation time.

nhl.goalie_quality.label: Goalie quality: goals saved above expected (GSAx), danger-zone save rates, workload-adjusted
nhl.goalie_quality.mechanism: A goalie's ability to save shots beyond what shot quality predicts directly changes goals against and the probability a given shot becomes a goal.
nhl.goalie_quality.rationale: GSAx removes shot-quality noise but is extremely noisy per goalie per season; true talent differences are smaller than they appear and shrinkage is mandatory. Subtle: the signal is mostly in high-danger and rebound control and differs by shot type; a small multi-year prior outperforms single-season numbers, and backup goalies have small samples.
nhl.goalie_quality.measurement: GSAx/60 and sv% by danger bucket over 2-3 seasons with exponential weights, shrunk toward league (Bayesian beta-binomial or empirical Bayes with prior strength ~1000-2000 shots); keep separate 5v5 and PK; adjust for team defence via on-ice xG model fitted with goalie fixed effect.

nhl.lines.label: Line combinations and defence pairings (forward lines, D pairs, PP/PK units)
nhl.lines.mechanism: Which skaters play together determines each player's linemates, shooting opportunities and quality of competition, which drives individual production independent of team strength.
nhl.lines.rationale: Line deployment explains much of the variation between players of equal talent, and lines change with injuries, scratches, and in-game coaching tweaks. Subtle: projected lines from the morning skate can differ from the puck-drop lines, coaches shuffle after losses and in third periods, and a 'line' list does not give minutes without a coach-specific deployment model.

nhl.toi.label: Projected time on ice by strength state (EV, PP, PK, late-game)
nhl.toi.mechanism: TOI by situation is the volume multiplier for every counting stat: more minutes (especially PP) means more shots, points and saves opportunities.
nhl.toi.rationale: Individual shots, points and assists scale nearly linearly with TOI; the key is the split by strength state because PP minutes are worth much more per minute than EV minutes. Subtle: TOI is partly endogenous to the score (stars play more when trailing), to penalties drawn and to coach decisions, so a pregame projection must be from the specific lineup and expected game script, not season average.
nhl.toi.measurement: Rolling EWMA TOI per strength state (last 10-20 games) conditioned on lineup (who is in/out), with adjustments for expected penalties and expected score script; model TOI by state as separate counts then sum; record projected-vs-actual error.

nhl.pp_role.label: Power-play unit assignment (PP1/PP2) and role (shooter/quarterback/net-front)
nhl.pp_role.mechanism: PP1 skaters get most PP time and the highest-leverage shot/assist roles on the man advantage, which produces a disproportionate share of points and shots.
nhl.pp_role.rationale: A PP1 quarterback or bumper position carries high point and shot rates per minute; PP2 players get far less. Roles matter within the unit: the one-timer position takes shots, the quarterback assists. Subtle: PP1 changes on injury/slump and is not announced, PP minutes are drawn opportunistically so the unit's expected PP minutes depend on the referee and opponent discipline.

nhl.shot_rate.label: Individual shot-attempt / SOG rate (per 60) by strength state
nhl.shot_rate.mechanism: A player's shot generation rate is a stable skill/role trait and, multiplied by TOI, gives expected shots on goal.
nhl.shot_rate.rationale: Individual shot rates are among the most repeatable player stats, far more than goals. Subtle: SOG differs from attempts by block and miss rates (shot type, defender, position), and SOG counts vary by rink scorer; rates must be split by EV/PP and shrunk, and recomputed after linemate changes.

nhl.finishing.label: Shooting percentage / finishing talent (regressed)
nhl.finishing.mechanism: Conversion of shots into goals is a mixture of shooter skill and luck; the skill part is small and persistent, the rest is noise that should regress.
nhl.finishing.rationale: Overweighting a hot shooting% inflates goal and point projections for players on lucky runs and underweights hidden talent for elite shooters. Subtle: true shooting talent is shot-quality adjusted (xG per shot), so compare goals to ixG to identify skill; sample sizes for individual shooters need multi-season data.
nhl.finishing.measurement: Compute goals minus individual xG and shot-quality-adjusted SH%; shrink with beta prior (about 200-300 shots for forwards) toward position mean plus a persistent-skill component estimated from multi-season repeatability; use predicted SH% not raw.

nhl.injuries_pit.label: Injury/scratch/return status with point-in-time vintages
nhl.injuries_pit.mechanism: Absences change line composition, ice time, power-play roles and opponent matchups, and a late scratch can void or zero a player prop.

nhl.opp_supp.label: Opponent shot suppression / goals-against by player position
nhl.opp_supp.mechanism: How many shots and points an opponent allows to a given position type scales the expected output of the player facing them.
nhl.opp_supp.rationale: Opponent adjustment for individual markets must be position-aware: a defence that allows many point shots inflates defencemen SOG, a team that blocks lots of shots reduces SOG per attempt. Subtle: opponent effects are small relative to player and role effects and noisy, so apply as shrunk multiplicative factors, not raw rank.
nhl.opp_supp.measurement: Estimate opponent effect on shots by player position (F/D) via mixed model: player-game SOG ~ player effect + opponent effect + home + TOI; shrink opponent random effects; use rolling window of 40-60 games; include opponent block rate and shot-attempt volume allowed.

nhl.rest_travel.label: Rest, back-to-back, travel distance/time zone, schedule density
nhl.rest_travel.mechanism: Fatigue and compressed schedules reduce skater performance and shift goalie starts to backups, which changes team strength and saves.
nhl.rest_travel.rationale: The most reliable schedule effects in NHL are back-to-back second games (more backup goalies, slightly worse results) and long road trips. Subtle: market prices largely incorporate rest, so the residual edge is in interactions (backup goalie probability, which team is rested while the other is tired, travel from different time zones) rather than the simple flag.

nhl.venue.label: Rink effects (shot counting bias), home advantage, building specifics
nhl.venue.mechanism: Different arenas record shots, hits and takeaways at different rates, and home teams see small advantages (last change, crowd, referees).
nhl.venue.rationale: Rink scorer bias inflates or deflates shot and SOG counts by arena; since SOG props settle on official counts, this is a pure measurement effect worth several percent. Subtle: bias is estimated from visiting teams' stats across venues and shifts with scorer turnover, and home advantage in hockey is modest and partly driven by last-change matchups.
nhl.venue.measurement: Estimate venue-specific shot-count multipliers via fixed-effects model on visiting teams' SOG per 60 across venues; use team-venue-season random effect; add home-ice indicator and altitude (Denver, Utah) as controls.

nhl.score_state.label: Game-script / score effects on shot volume, quality and pulled-goalie behavior
nhl.score_state.mechanism: Teams trailing push shot volume and risk, teams leading play defensive structures, changing shot totals and shot quality within the same game.
nhl.score_state.rationale: Shot counts for the favourite and for stars depend on expected game script: a heavy favourite often leads and accumulates fewer SOG late, while the underdog trailing generates more attempts but lower quality. Subtle: the pregame uncertainty over script means player-shot distributions are mixtures over win-probability scenarios, not shift in the mean alone.
nhl.score_state.measurement: Estimate shot rate and xG per 60 by score state (down 2+, down 1, tied, up 1, up 2+) per team, then integrate over the game-script distribution implied by pregame win probability and total (simulation); report adjusted rates for 'neutral' state to avoid circularity.

nhl.ot_so.label: Overtime and shootout model and rules
nhl.ot_so.mechanism: Overtime and shootout resolve regulation ties through a different structure (3v3 sudden death, then skill contest), which sets the final outcome for markets that include them.
nhl.ot_so.rationale: Settlement wording decides whether overtime/shootout counts; for including-OT markets the winner is a function of regulation-tie probability and OT/SO win probability (near coin-flip with small team-strength tilt). Subtle: regular-season OT is 5-minute 3v3 followed by shootout, playoffs are full 20-minute 5v5 periods with no shootout, so the same code must branch by season type; OT goal totals contribute to total-goals markets only if rules include them.

nhl.empty_net.label: Empty-net goals and pulled-goalie timing
nhl.empty_net.mechanism: Trailing teams pull the goalie late, generating empty-net goals for the leader and extra shots for the trailer, which moves totals, margins and goalie saves.
nhl.empty_net.rationale: Empty-net goals add to the total in some close games, are strongly correlated with close margins, and affect puck-line (the leader wins by 2) and saves markets. Subtle: pull timing differs by coach (earlier pulls increase both EN goals against and chances), and a goal scored into an empty net may count toward totals but not for goalie stats.

nhl.period_split.label: Period-level scoring and shot distribution
nhl.period_split.mechanism: Goals and shots are not uniform across periods: the second period (long change) and third (score effects) behave differently from the first.
nhl.period_split.rationale: Period markets need period-specific rates, not one-third of the full game. Subtle: first periods usually have lower scoring and fewer penalties, third periods have empty-net goals and score effects, and the 2nd period long-change effect increases scoring chances against away team in the middle frame in some analyses; use team-specific period splits shrunk strongly toward league period shape.
nhl.period_split.measurement: Estimate league period shape of goals/shots by season; team-specific multiplicative deviations via hierarchical model with heavy shrinkage; produce Poisson/negative-binomial period distributions and joint period correlation.

nhl.stat_dist.label: Per-stat count distributions and correlations (Poisson/NB, joint)
nhl.stat_dist.mechanism: Counts (shots, points, saves) are overdispersed discrete variables whose full distribution, not just the mean, determines threshold-rung probabilities.
nhl.stat_dist.rationale: Threshold markets depend on tail probabilities, which are controlled by dispersion and by correlation with game total and team results. Subtle: simple Poisson underestimates variance for shots driven by script and TOI uncertainty; zero-inflated or mixed distributions fit points better; correlation across a player's goals, assists, shots matters for combined markets and parlay legs.
nhl.stat_dist.measurement: Fit per-stat count models (NB or compound Poisson with TOI uncertainty) to player-game history with covariates; estimate dispersion via likelihood; compute joint correlation matrices by simulation within games; validate against realized rung frequencies.

nhl.ratings.label: Team ratings, standings and season simulation
nhl.ratings.mechanism: A calibrated team rating system turns game-level strength into win probabilities and into season simulations for futures.
nhl.ratings.rationale: Futures and series prices depend on the distribution of team strength and its uncertainty, not just point estimates; ratings must update for injuries and trades. Subtle: points standings contain heavy luck (OT, shootouts, shooting%), so xG-based or goal-differential ratings are preferable and tie-break rules (regulation wins) affect seeding.
nhl.ratings.measurement: Elo or Bradley-Terry/Poisson ratings fit on score-adjusted xG differential with home and goalie terms, exponential time decay, shrinkage to preseason priors, then Monte Carlo season simulation using actual remaining schedule and NHL tie-break rules.

m.quote_history.label: Kalshi bid/ask/last time series (pre-game through close)
m.quote_history.mechanism: The traded price aggregates every participant's information about this contract, including injury and lineup news that moves faster than public stats.
m.quote_history.rationale: A price series is both a feature (the late price is usually a strong prior that model inputs must add to, not replace) and the reference for any edge claim. Subtle: the same last-trade price can be stale on thin NHL prop rungs, so bid/ask midpoints with timestamps matter more than last, and price movement after lineup/goalie/pitcher confirmation is information about what the news was worth.
m.quote_history.measurement: Store per-ticker candlesticks (bid, ask, last, volume) at 1-minute or finer resolution, align to scheduled start and to timestamps of lineup/starter confirmation; derive mid, spread, move since open, move since confirmation. Never use post-close values as pregame features.

m.orderbook_depth.label: Order-book depth and spread
m.orderbook_depth.mechanism: Depth and spread determine whether a modelled edge can be executed and how much the quoted price reflects informed versus noise flow.
m.orderbook_depth.rationale: Wide spreads and thin depth on NHL prop and long-tail rungs mean the midpoint is a noisy probability estimate and the edge after crossing the spread may be negative. Subtle: historical depth is only available if captured live, so the pregame view is whatever was snapshotted; reconstructing it from trades is approximate.
m.orderbook_depth.measurement: Snapshot the book (top-N levels both sides) at fixed intervals before start; compute spread, depth within 2 cents of mid, imbalance. Compare model edge to half-spread plus fee to get executable edge.

m.volume_oi.label: Volume and open interest
m.volume_oi.mechanism: Volume and open interest proxy for how many participants have priced the contract and therefore how efficient the price is likely to be.
m.volume_oi.rationale: High-volume markets (game winners, totals) are typically priced by more informed flow than thin player props; a model needs a different shrinkage toward the market in each regime. Subtle: volume surges in the final hour often coincide with lineup news and are not directional by themselves.
m.volume_oi.measurement: Cumulative and last-hour volume, open interest, number of distinct trades from the trade tape; bucket markets by liquidity tier and estimate market-vs-model weight per tier.

m.ladder_structure.label: Cross-rung consistency of the threshold ladder (monotonicity, implied distribution)
m.ladder_structure.mechanism: Rungs of a threshold ladder (e.g. 4+, 5+, 6+) must imply one coherent count distribution; deviations expose stale or mispriced rungs and reveal the market's implied mean and variance.
m.ladder_structure.rationale: Ladders for the same player/game are strongly correlated, so edges on adjacent rungs are not independent bets and exposure must be sized per ladder. Subtle: because each rung is a survival probability P(X>=k), monotone non-increasing is a hard constraint, and fitting a Poisson/negative-binomial to the rungs gives an implied mean that can be compared to a model mean on a like-for-like basis.
m.ladder_structure.measurement: For each event/player collect all live rungs at one timestamp; check P(k) non-increasing; fit a discrete distribution (Poisson, negative binomial, or free-form isotonic) to mid prices; compare implied mean/variance and per-rung residual to the model; track which rungs the market lags when news arrives.

m.settlement_truth.label: Settled result, settlement value and timestamp

m.settlement_truth.rationale: Without exact settlement values, hit rates and calibration are computed against a proxy (box score) that may differ from Kalshi's source (official stats, correction windows). m.settlement_truth.measurement: Join Kalshi settled result and settlement_value to the official box score by game id; flag disagreements and post-game scoring changes; keep settlement time minus game end time.

m.rules_text.rationale: Identical-looking contracts can differ: whether overtime/extra innings counts, whether a player who does not play voids or settles at zero, how postponements and shortened games resolve, which official stat source governs. m.external_lines.label: Sportsbook / exchange reference prices with timestamps
m.external_lines.mechanism: Sharp sportsbook and exchange lines are a competing aggregation of information and the standard benchmark for fair probability.
m.external_lines.rationale: Using a de-vigged external line as a feature or benchmark is often a stronger baseline than any public-stats model, and disagreement with Kalshi flags either a stale Kalshi quote or a rule-wording difference. Subtle: books price different settlement terms (e.g. regulation vs including overtime, 'action' rules on postponements) so lines must be mapped to the Kalshi rule before comparison, and the timestamp of the line matters.
m.external_lines.measurement: Capture timestamped lines per book; de-vig (power or Shin method) per market; map to the Kalshi contract's rule (regulation vs full game, push handling); compute Kalshi minus consensus and closing-line value relative to the latest pregame consensus.

m.fees.label: Fee schedule and maker/taker rules in force

m.fees.rationale: Because the fee is price-dependent, a fixed edge in cents is worth less near 50 than at the tails or vice versa depending on schedule; a model signal must clear fee-adjusted breakeven, not raw midpoint difference. Subtle: fee schedules change over time and by market type, so the version in force at trade time must be used.
m.fees.measurement: Version the fee formula from Kalshi's published fee schedule; compute breakeven probability per price and role; subtract from model edge before any threshold decision.

m.lifecycle.label: Open/close/halt/postponement lifecycle events

m.strike_hit_rates.label: Historical realized frequency by strike/rung per family (from settlements)
m.strike_hit_rates.mechanism: Realized frequency by rung gives the unconditional base rate that every conditional model must beat, and reveals persistent biases in how thresholds are set.
m.strike_hit_rates.rationale: Markets often over- or under-price specific rung shapes (round-number thresholds, longshot tails). Base rates by rung, season, venue and liquidity tier reveal where the market is calibrated and where it is not. Subtle: settled history is selection-biased by which strikes Kalshi chose to list, so rates are conditional on being listed.
m.strike_hit_rates.measurement: From settled markets compute hit rate by family x strike x price bucket with confidence intervals; compare to implied price; keep season and rule-version splits.

m.trade_tape.label: Executed trades (price, size, taker side, time) for slippage and flow
m.trade_tape.mechanism: Executed trades reveal where size actually transacted, the taker side, and the speed at which price reacts to news.
m.trade_tape.rationale: Trade flow around lineup/goalie/pitcher confirmation shows how quickly information is incorporated; sustained one-sided taker flow can indicate informed trading. Subtle: only executed prints are observable, resting orders are not, so slippage estimates from the tape understate the cost of crossing a thin book.

nhl.season_sim_distribution.label: Season simulation distribution (points, playoffs, division)
nhl.season_sim_distribution.mechanism: Season markets are tails of an 82-game simulation including overtime-point rules and injury uncertainty.
nhl.season_sim_distribution.rationale: NHL standings points are 2-1-0 with overtime-loss points, so points markets need a bivariate result model, not just win probability. Subtle: goalie injuries and back-to-back starts alter win probability game by game.
nhl.season_sim_distribution.measurement: Monte Carlo from own expected-goals ratings with goalie-state uncertainty, regulation/overtime split and wildcard tiebreakers; report points and playoff distributions.

nhl.third_period_equalizer_hazard.label: Late-game equalizer and empty-net hazard by team and coach
nhl.third_period_equalizer_hazard.mechanism: Converts a one-goal late deficit into tie or two-goal-loss outcomes using 6v5 rates and the coach's pull time.
nhl.third_period_equalizer_hazard.rationale: The existing empty_net input is a single bucket for 'pulled-goalie timing'; for tie probability the two competing outcomes of a pull (equalizer vs empty-net goal against) and their dependence on pull time are what move the diagonal of the score distribution. Pull time has drifted earlier league-wide and differs by coach.
nhl.third_period_equalizer_hazard.measurement: From play-by-play, for every regular-season and playoff game since 2015-16 find states with the trailing team down exactly one goal and the goalie pulled; per team-coach compute (a) median pull time in seconds remaining, (b) equalizer rate = goals for per 60 minutes of 6v5 time, (c) empty-net goals against per 60 of 6v5 time. Shrink each to league with k=20 pulls, weight seasons with 2-year half-life, and reset on a coaching change. Output pregame P(equalizer | trailing by 1 at T-3:00) and P(EN | trailing by 1) per team pair.

nhl.ot_sudden_death_hazard_5v5.label: [Playoff-only, dormant for KXNHLOT] 5v5 sudden-death overtime goal hazard (playoff OT)
nhl.ot_sudden_death_hazard_5v5.mechanism: Hazard of a goal per 20-minute playoff overtime period at 5v5 given tied score, fatigue and style.
nhl.ot_sudden_death_hazard_5v5.rationale: Playoff overtime is 5v5 sudden death in 20-minute periods, not the 3v3 of the regular season, so the existing 3v3 rate does not transfer; double-OT markets depend on the first period producing no goal, which has a different hazard than 60-minute rates imply.
nhl.ot_sudden_death_hazard_5v5.measurement: Pool all playoff OT minutes since 2005-06 (about 450 games) at 5v5 and compute the goal rate per 60 for tied score; model hazard h(t) = h0 x tied-game 5v5 multiplier x team-pair factor, where the team-pair factor is the geometric mean of both teams' tied 5v5 xG rate shrunk to league with k=500 minutes. Fatigue multiplier estimated from period index (OT1 vs OT2) and rest differential. P(no goal in OT1) = exp(-h x 20/60). Do not use regular-season 3v3 minutes.

nhl.series_ot_count_dependence.label: [Playoff-only, dormant until KXNHL2OT/KXNHLSERIESOT list markets] Within-series dependence of overtime occurrence
nhl.series_ot_count_dependence.mechanism: Intraclass correlation of per-game tie indicators within the same playoff series.
nhl.series_ot_count_dependence.rationale: Games in one series share goalies, coaches and defensive structure, so OT counts are overdispersed relative to independent Bernoulli; a binomial series-OT price is too thin-tailed.
nhl.series_ot_count_dependence.measurement: Fit a beta-binomial to the count of games reaching OT in each historical playoff series (2005-06 onward, series lengths 4-7 handled by conditioning on length), estimate overdispersion rho; then per series set p_game = reg_tie_model pregame tie probability and apply rho to get the pmf of OT-game count. Update rho with a prior of 0.05 and k=40 series.

nhl.tied_late_risk_posture.label: Tied-game closing posture (late risk aversion when a point is banked)
nhl.tied_late_risk_posture.mechanism: Change in late 5v5 attempt share and danger in tied games relative to earlier tied-game play.
nhl.tied_late_risk_posture.rationale: A tied third period guarantees a standings point, which may lower risk-taking; if present it raises P(OT) above what 60-minute rates give. It is a hypothesis to measure, not an assumed effect.
nhl.tied_late_risk_posture.measurement: For each team and season compute shot-attempt share and high-danger attempts per 60 at 5v5 in the final 5:00 of regulation when the score is tied, minus the same team's rate in minutes 40:00-55:00 when tied; shrink to league with k=60 tied-late minutes and report per-team posture index; interact with standings leverage (points pct within 4 of a cutoff). Add the minimum of two teams' indices as the pair posture.
free_sources: Natural Stat Trick score-and-time filtered splits

nhl.ratings_script_distribution.label: Ratings-only pregame score-path distribution (lead/trail/tied time shares and entering-state matrix)
nhl.ratings_script_distribution.mechanism: Simulated from team goal rates alone, the distribution of score states by period and the share of 60 minutes spent leading, trailing or tied shapes shot volume, star deployment, pull timing and empty-net goals without ever touching a price.
nhl.ratings_script_distribution.rationale: The catalog nhl.game_script_prob derives its win probability from ratings AND the market line, so it is contaminated by the benchmark. This replacement is built only from market-free inputs: it keeps the useful scenario-probability content (conditional state mixtures, not a single win probability) while leaving the market line as a comparison target. The subtle point is that the object needed is a distribution over states, not one number.
nhl.ratings_script_distribution.measurement: For each team, set expected 5v5 and special-teams goal rates for the game as lambda_i = league mean x (attack_i x defence_j adjusted xG ratings, shrunk with prior_to_current_blend where available, or ratings built from score-adjusted xGF/xGA per 60 over a 40-game EWMA with 20-game half-life shrunk 25 games toward league mean) x goalie factor (confirmed or probability-weighted starter GSAx per 60 shrunk 1000 shots) plus a home-ice constant estimated from the last 5 seasons. Simulate 20000 games with a negative-binomial goal process with the fitted dispersion, event times drawn from a time-varying rate with score effects, a pull rule at the coach-specific trailing time, and OT 3v3 play. Output per game: P(lead/tied/trail) entering each period, expected minutes in each score state, P(margin>=2 entering the third), and expected 6v5 minutes per team. As-of timestamp: latest ratings and confirmed or probabilistic starter before puck drop; never include any sportsbook or Kalshi price.
free_sources: Natural Stat Trick team game logs

nhl.settlement_goal_pmf.label: Settlement-adjusted final-margin distribution (regulation, OT, shootout, empty net)
nhl.settlement_goal_pmf.mechanism: Maps team goal-rate parameters to the full pmf of final margin under official scoring rules.
nhl.settlement_goal_pmf.rationale: Moneyline, spread and regulation-winner contracts read different functionals of one distribution; building each from its own ad hoc model creates inconsistent prices. The pmf must apply: regulation bivariate counts, late empty-net transitions, an OT goal as a one-goal margin, and a shootout as a one-goal margin with a near-even winner.
nhl.settlement_goal_pmf.measurement: Simulate or enumerate: regulation (H, A) from fitted bivariate overdispersed counts at 55:00 plus a final-5-minute jump process using team pull-time and 6v5 rates; if tied at 60:00 draw OT with 3v3 goal hazard (regular season) giving +/-1 margin, else shootout winner with p = 0.5 + shrunk team SO talent (k=60 attempts) giving +/-1. Output P(margin >= m) for m=1..6 per team and P(regulation tie). Validate by reproducing the league margin histogram (about 25 percent one-goal games) per season.

nhl.lineup_impact_delta.label: Lineup impact delta from player value model (skater and goalie)
nhl.lineup_impact_delta.mechanism: Converts who is in or out into a change in expected goal difference using per-player impact estimates.
nhl.lineup_impact_delta.rationale: Injury status flags tell who is missing but not what it costs; a top-pair defenceman, a first-line centre and a starting goalie have different values, and replacements play different minutes. The cost must be computed from minutes redistributed times impact difference.
nhl.lineup_impact_delta.measurement: Estimate per-skater impact as regularised adjusted xG per 60 at 5v5 (ridge RAPM on shift-level data, 3-season window, half-life 1.5 seasons, shrink toward position mean) plus special-teams impact per PP/PK minute; for the projected lineup compute delta = sum_over_players(proj_TOI_new x impact_new) minus same for base lineup, restated as goals per 60 and then x 60/60 per game; for goalies use shrunk GSAx per 1000 shots (k=2000 shots) scaled by opponent shot volume. As-of rule: use lineups published by the team at the time of prediction; keep prior vintages.

nhl.prior_to_current_blend.label: Preseason prior blend weight by games played
nhl.prior_to_current_blend.mechanism: Weights current-season data against a preseason prior as a function of sample size.
nhl.prior_to_current_blend.rationale: At this point in the season (early November) a team has played about 12-15 games; xG share has a stabilisation point of several dozen games, so raw current xG overstates differences and ignores roster turnover.
nhl.prior_to_current_blend.measurement: Prior = last two seasons' score-adjusted rating (weights 0.6/0.4) adjusted by net roster change (minutes-weighted impact of arrivals minus departures) and age curve; posterior = (n x current + k x prior)/(n + k) with k in the 25-40 games range fit by minimising out-of-sample log loss of game result; recompute weekly. Report posterior sd to the simulator.

nhl.pp_termination_unit_split.label: Power-play termination and unit-time split
nhl.pp_termination_unit_split.mechanism: Expected PP goals per penalty given that a minor ends on a goal and PP1/PP2 share the clock.
nhl.pp_termination_unit_split.rationale: PP time is not additive: a two-minute minor ends when the power-play team scores, so goals per PP are concave in minutes, and the first unit plays roughly the first 60-80 seconds, so PP1 production dominates short power plays. Using PP time x rate overstates multi-goal PP games and misallocates credit among players.
nhl.pp_termination_unit_split.measurement: From play-by-play, for each team and season compute: (a) conversion per PP opportunity (minor penalties only, excluding coincident and 4v4 states), (b) hazard of a PP goal as a function of elapsed PP seconds in 15-second bins, (c) PP1 share of PP time as a function of elapsed seconds, (d) PP goal share by unit. Shrink team hazard to league with k=150 PP opportunities and 2-season half-life. Expected PP goals = sum over expected penalties of integral hazard x survival; keep major and double-minor cases separate.

nhl.pair_attempt_volume.label: Pair attempt-volume composite (log-additive team tempo model)
nhl.pair_attempt_volume.mechanism: Expected combined attempts from offence-for and defence-against terms fit jointly.
nhl.pair_attempt_volume.rationale: Combined pace is not the average of the two teams' season paces: each team's attempts depend on its own offence and the opponent's suppression and on score effects, and the two teams' counts are correlated through game state. A pair composite avoids double counting.
nhl.pair_attempt_volume.measurement: Fit a Poisson regression of 5v5 attempts per 60 for each team-game: log E = mu + off_team + def_opp + home + score-state adjustment, with ridge penalty and 2-season half-life; game attempts = sum of both teams' predictions x projected 5v5 minutes (60 minus expected PP/PK minutes). Add pair random effect with variance estimated from residual covariance. Evaluate pace-weighted xG, not raw attempts, when converting to goals.

nhl.opp_sog_for_rate.label: Opponent shots-on-goal-for rate by strength state, score adjusted
nhl.opp_sog_for_rate.mechanism: Opponent's own shot-on-goal generation per 60 at EV and on the power play.
nhl.opp_sog_for_rate.rationale: The draft carries opponent xG (a quality measure) and the defence's suppression, but saves count shots on goal, so the opponent's volume of on-target shots, separate from danger, is the first-order driver. xG weights shots by quality and understates the effect of low-danger volume teams.
nhl.opp_sog_for_rate.measurement: Per team compute SOG for per 60 at 5v5 (score-and-venue adjusted via regression of SOG rate on score differential bins) and at 5v4, with 2-season half-life 40 games and shrink to league with k=15 games; project game SOG faced = EV_rate_opp x defence_adjustment x projected EV minutes + PP_rate_opp x projected PP minutes. Use log-additive combination with opponent defence SOG-against: log E = mu + off_opp + def_team.
